publisher.title: Publisher of the site

director.title: Publication director
director.body:
The publication director is Mr {{publisherRepresentative}}, in his capacity as manager of {{publisherName}}. He can be reached by post at the registered office or by e-mail at {{publisherEmail}}.

DIASPORA has no editorial staff. Information published in the name of the network (team announcements, rules, help pages) is published under the responsibility of the publisher. Other content is published by members and by the pages of associations and companies, under their own responsibility.

hosting.title: Hosting and technical providers
hosting.body:
The web application is served by Vercel Inc., 440 N Barranca Avenue #4133, Covina, CA 91723, United States of America.

The network’s database, files and server functions are run on the infrastructure of Convex, Inc., a company established in the United States of America.

DIASPORA is an application of the ANTSIA social engine, published by the same company: a single account serves both networks.

The Privacy page gives the list of providers that process data, their role and the rules governing transfers outside Gabon. Any change of provider is recorded here and on that page, with a new version of the text.

service.title: Nature of the service
service.body:
DIASPORA is a closed social network, reserved for Gabonese citizens living outside Gabon. It is published by a private company: it is neither a service of the Gabonese State nor a service of an embassy or consulate. No consular procedure is handled on it and no official document is issued on it.

Membership is free. DIASPORA collects no payment and shows no advertising.

The network falls under the High Authority for Communication (HAC) for its content, and under the Authority for the Protection of Personal Data and Privacy (APDPVP) for personal data.

intellectualProperty.title: Intellectual property
intellectualProperty.body:
The name DIASPORA, its logo, its graphic identity, its interfaces, its texts and the software that runs the network belong to {{publisherName}} or are used with the consent of their owners. They are protected by Law No. 1/87 of 29 July 1987 on copyright and neighbouring rights and by the Bangui Agreement, which establishes the African Intellectual Property Organization (OAPI).

Any reproduction, representation or adaptation of these elements without the written consent of the publisher is prohibited, except in the cases the law allows and within the limits of the licences under which the publisher releases some of its software.

Content published by members and by pages remains the property of its authors. The Terms of use say what publishing it allows.

illegalContent.title: Reporting illegal content
illegalContent.body:
Every item of content on the network has a “Report” action. A person who is not a member can write to the publisher at {{publisherEmail}}, giving the address of the content, what they object to and a way to reach them.

The publisher promptly removes manifestly illegal content as soon as it becomes aware of it. The Community rules describe how a report is handled, its time limits and the appeals.

rightOfReply.title: Right of reply
rightOfReply.body:
Any person named in content on the network has a right of reply (Ordinance No. 0011/PR/2026, Articles 26 and 27).

The request is sent to the publisher, by e-mail or by post to the registered office, within three months of publication. It identifies the content concerned and gives the text of the reply. The reply is inserted within 48 hours of receipt of a valid request; where the content comes from a member or a page, the publisher forwards the request to them.

personalData.title: Personal data
personalData.body:
{{publisherName}} is the controller of members’ personal data. This processing is governed by Law No. 001/2011 of 25 September 2011 on the protection of personal data, as amended by Law No. 025/2023 of 12 July 2023, under the supervision of the APDPVP.

The Privacy page says what data is processed, why, for how long, who receives it and how to exercise your rights.

contact.title: Contacting us
contact.body:
For any question about the service, write to {{publisherEmail}} or to {{publisherName}}, {{publisherAddress}}.

The Contact page gives the direct route to report content, exercise your rights over your data or refer a matter to a supervisory authority.

law.title: Applicable law

controller.title: Data controller
controller.body:
The controller of your data is {{publisherName}}, a limited liability company under Gabonese law, {{publisherAddress}} (RCCM {{publisherRccm}}), publisher of DIASPORA and of the ANTSIA engine.

For any question about your data, write to {{publisherEmail}} or by post to the registered office, stating “Personal data — DIASPORA”.

This page describes what the service does today. As your account is shared by DIASPORA and ANTSIA, export and erasure apply to the whole account.

framework.title: Legal framework
framework.body:
The processing of your data is governed by Law No. 001/2011 of 25 September 2011 on the protection of personal data, as amended by Law No. 025/2023 of 12 July 2023, under the supervision of the Authority for the Protection of Personal Data and Privacy (APDPVP). That Law covers processing carried out by a controller established in Gabon (Article 4): it protects you whatever your country of residence.

If you live in the European Union, Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) also applies, because the network is addressed to people who live there (Article 3). Where the two texts differ, the rule that protects you most is applied.

The Law requires this processing to be declared to the APDPVP (Articles 78 and 175), and transfers of data outside Gabon to be authorised by it (Article 171). The number of the receipt issued by the Authority will be shown on this page.

Ordinance No. 0011/PR/2026 of 26 February 2026 on the use of social networks, ratified by Law No. 003/2026 of 5 October 2026, also sets obligations specific to social networks: identification of the publisher, protection of minors, time limits for handling reports.

data.title: The data we process
data.body:
We process only the data needed for the network to work (Law No. 001/2011 as amended, Article 70). It comes from you, unless stated otherwise.

– Account and sign-in: your e-mail address, one-time sign-in codes (kept only as a hash, valid for 5 minutes) and your sessions. There is no password.
– Digital identity: if you sign in through identite.ga, that service sends us, with the consent you give it, your identifier, your verified e-mail address, your name, the assurance level of your identity, your nationality and your profile type. To establish your status, we keep only the identifier, the assurance level, the nationality and the profile type; the technical tokens of that sign-in are kept with your account. To suggest a display name and a handle when you enter, we also keep your name and handles derived from your identite.ga identifier, for 24 hours at most: they are shown to you before your profile is created, you can change them, and they are erased as soon as your profile is created.
– Profile: display name, public handle, tagline, photo and banner, language, time zone, chosen appearance.
– Situation in the diaspora: country of residence (required) and, if you provide them, city, consular post of attachment, associations, year of arrival, availability to help.
– Membership: status, date of entry, sponsor, sponsorships given, suspension measures.
– Consents: for each purpose, the version of the text accepted, the date of consent and the date of its withdrawal.
– Content: posts, comments, reactions, statuses, albums, saved posts, photos and videos uploaded. Information hidden in a photo, such as where it was taken, is removed before upload.
– Connections: requests and connections, follows, blocks, mutes.
– Messages: personal and group messages, attachments, read receipts. Messages are not end-to-end encrypted. The moderation team does not look at your conversations; it examines a message only if it is reported.
– Notifications: the list of your notifications, your preferences and, if you turn on device notifications, your browser’s subscription address.
– Pages: for the pages you run, the page information, your role and, in the case of a claim, the supporting documents provided.
– Moderation: reports you make or that concern you, decisions, measures and appeals.
– Technical data: session identifiers, browser type, counters used to limit abuse. As with any site, delivering pages passes your IP address through our technical providers; the network does not use it to build a profile.

The spaces that will open later (groups and events, services, jobs, mutual aid, mentoring) will process the data you enter there; each will ask for its own consent where one is needed.

neverCollected.title: What we do not process

purposes.title: Why we process it

consents.title: Your consents
consents.body:
Each consent is separate and dated. You can withdraw it at any time in your settings, without affecting what was done before the withdrawal (Law No. 001/2011 as amended, Articles 72 and 73). No consent is given in advance on your behalf: each one comes from an action of yours.

– Social profile: your display name, your handle and your country are visible to members. You give this consent by pressing “Create my profile and enter”, below the sentence that says what members will see; the name and handle suggested from identite.ga are shown to you first, and you can change them. This is the only consent required: without it, there is no membership.
– Directory: you are hidden from it by default. After you enter, it is offered to you by a separate action, and you choose who can find you there, between no one, the members of your country and the whole network.
– Notifications: off by default. After you enter, they are offered to you by a separate action. A notification never carries the content of a message.
– Consular attestation: a request for confirmation from consulat.ga, when that service opens.
– Talents: display of your professional profile, when the jobs space opens.

Some actions ask for their own consent at the moment you take them, for example publishing a review or passing your identity to the author of an offer.

visibility.title: Who sees what
visibility.body:
You decide the audience for each item of information.

– Profile: the display name, the handle and the country of residence are visible to members. For other information, you choose between yourself only, your connections, the members of your country and the whole network. By default, the city is visible only to your connections; the consular post, the associations and the year of arrival are visible only to you.
– Posts: readable by the members of DIASPORA, or reserved for your connections. They are readable in ANTSIA, the public network, only if you decide so.
– Messages: read by you and your correspondents.
– Contact details: your e-mail address is never displayed or passed on to another member.
– Outside the network: DIASPORA is closed, and its pages are not offered to search engines.

Authorised members of the moderation team and of the publisher access only the information needed for their task; their administration decisions are logged.

recipients.title: Recipients and providers

transfers.title: Transfers outside Gabon
transfers.body:
Convex, Inc., Vercel Inc. and Resend, Inc. are established in the United States of America, and the notification services belong to the browser publishers: data is therefore processed outside Gabon.

The Law makes these transfers subject to the authorisation of the APDPVP and to the existence of sufficient safeguards (Law No. 001/2011 as amended, Articles 171 and 173). They rest on the contractual commitments of these providers on confidentiality and security, and are limited to what the operation of the service requires.

If you live in the European Union, your data is likewise processed outside the Union, by the publisher and by these providers.

retention.title: Retention periods

security.title: Security

rights.title: Your rights

exercise.title: Exercising your rights

minors.title: Minors
minors.body:
DIASPORA is reserved for adults. We do not knowingly process the data of a person under 18: the Law makes such processing subject to the consent of their parents (Law No. 001/2011 as amended, Articles 74 and 190) and prohibits the creation of any account before the age of 16 (Ordinance No. 0011/PR/2026, Articles 16 and 17).

If you think a minor has opened an account, report their profile or write to the publisher: the account is closed and its data is erased. The parent of a minor under 16 can request this erasure themselves (Ordinance No. 0011/PR/2026, Article 14).

cookies.title: Cookies and storage on your device

automated.title: Feed, suggestions and automated decisions
automated.body:
The feed arranges posts by date, from the most recent to the oldest. It takes into account neither your clicks nor your reading time, and no profile is built from your activity. The menu of a post tells you why it is shown to you.

No decision that produces effects on you is taken by fully automated processing. Automatic limits (writing rate, number of links, blocked terms) may hold back a piece of content; every moderation measure is decided by a person.

The network uses no artificial intelligence system to analyse your content or your messages.

breach.title: In the event of a data breach
breach.body: If a data breach occurs, the publisher informs the APDPVP without delay (Law No. 001/2011 as amended, Article 142). Where it puts your rights at high risk, you are informed as soon as possible, with the measures taken and those you can take (Articles 145 to 147).

complaint.title: Complaints

changes.title: Changes to this page
changes.body: This page carries a version number and a date. It is updated when the service changes: a new provider, a new space, a new retention period. A significant change is announced in the network; where it affects processing based on your consent, your consent is asked for again.

purpose.title: Purpose

acceptance.title: Acceptance
acceptance.body:
Creating an account, entering the network or continuing to use it amounts to acceptance of these terms and of the Community rules. If you do not accept them, do not use the service: you can leave the network or request the erasure of your account at any time, from “My data”.

Accepting these terms is not consenting to the processing of your data. The only consent requested on entry, the social profile, is presented to you separately, right above the “Create my profile and enter” button that gives it; the others (directory, notifications, consular attestation…) are requested later, each by a distinct action. You can withdraw each one whenever you wish (Law No. 001/2011 as amended, Articles 72 and 73).

access.title: Access to the network

account.title: Your account
account.body:
One account per person. It is personal: you do not lend it, you do not transfer it and you do not open a second one.

Your account is an ANTSIA account, the public network of which DIASPORA is a closed network: entering DIASPORA creates your membership of ANTSIA, and a suspension imposed in ANTSIA applies in DIASPORA. What you publish in DIASPORA stays there, unless you yourself choose to make it readable in ANTSIA.

You sign in with a one-time code received by e-mail, or with your identite.ga digital identity. There is no password. Keep control of your inbox and never share a code: no one, not even the network’s team, will ask you for it.

You provide accurate information and keep it up to date, in particular your country of residence. The Law requires every account holder to identify themselves (Ordinance No. 0011/PR/2026, Article 4): the publisher may ask you to confirm or complete your identification.

You are responsible for the use made of your account. If you think another person has access to it, close all your sessions using “Sign out everywhere” and notify the publisher.

free.title: Free of charge
free.body:
Membership and use of the network are free for members. DIASPORA collects no payment, takes no commission on exchanges between members and shows no advertising. Internet connection costs remain your responsibility.

If paid services are ever offered to organisations, they will be separate, presented as such and subject to their own terms. A member will never pay to enter the network or to remain in it.

conduct.title: Rules of use

content.title: Your content
content.body:
You remain the owner of what you publish. By publishing, you grant the publisher a non-exclusive, free-of-charge right to keep your content, to reproduce it, to adapt it to technical formats and to display it to the audience you have chosen, worldwide and for as long as it is published. This right serves only to make the network work: the publisher does not sell your content and does not use it for advertising.

By default, a post is readable by the members of DIASPORA. You can reserve it for your connections. It is readable in ANTSIA only if you decide so.

You can remove content at any time: it is then removed everywhere it was distributed. Reported content may, however, be kept for the duration of the procedure, as the Law requires of the publisher.

You warrant that you have the right to publish what you publish: you are its author, or you have the consent of its author and of the people who appear in it.

If you publish an image, a sound or a video produced or altered by artificial intelligence that could pass for real, say so clearly in the post.

pages.title: Pages of associations and companies
pages.body:
A page presents an association or a company. Only a verified member can register one. The person who registers or claims a page declares that they are entitled to act in the name of the organisation.

Supporting documents may be requested in support of a claim. They are read only by the team in charge of examining it; they are deleted as soon as the request is withdrawn, or 90 days after the decision.

The managers of a page (administrator, editor, moderator) are responsible for what is published on it: they ensure the information is accurate, remove illegal content and respond to reports. The Law makes the administrator of a page or group responsible for the illegal content that circulates on it (Ordinance No. 0011/PR/2026, Article 11).

Its managers can put a page to sleep and wake it within 30 days; after that period, putting it back into service is decided with the network’s administration. A page that no longer has a manager, that misleads about the organisation it presents or that breaks the rules may be suspended or removed.

exchanges.title: Exchanges between members
exchanges.body:
The services, job offers, mutual aid assignments and introductions offered in the network are offered by members and by pages, under their sole responsibility. The publisher is not a party to any agreement concluded between members: it guarantees neither the reality of an offer, nor the quality of a service, nor the solvency of anyone.

No payment goes through DIASPORA. Never pay money to obtain a job, housing, a visa or an appointment, and report any request of that kind.

consular.title: Institutions and consular procedures
consular.body:
DIASPORA is not a consular service. No procedure (passport, consular card, civil status, visa) is handled on it, and the service does not ask you for an identity document, a passport number or a personal identification number. Do not publish them and do not send them to anyone through messaging.

When the consular registration attestation opens, it will be limited, with your consent, to a yes or no answer, a country, a consular post and a date. No other element of your consular file will enter the network.

An official page speaks in the name of the institution it presents. What a member publishes binds only that member, even if they work for an institution.

moderation.title: Moderation
moderation.body:
The network’s moderation team examines reports, under the authority of the network’s administration. The report of a profile, which is shared by DIASPORA and ANTSIA, is examined by ANTSIA moderation.

The publisher does not exercise general control before publication. Three means complement reports:

– some content is reviewed before it appears;
– automatic limits (number of links, writing rate, blocked terms) may hold content back until it is reviewed;
– uploaded files go through an antivirus scan.

No sanction is imposed by an automated system: every measure is decided by a person, who never rules on a case in which they are a party.

The possible measures are removal of the content, a warning, mute, suspension and exclusion. A mute or a suspension has a duration, of 365 days at most; an exclusion has none. Each decision is reasoned and notified to the person concerned, who can find it in “My data” and can appeal against it at two levels, with no time limit imposed.

The publisher carries out court decisions and the measures ordered by the competent authorities. It informs those authorities of illegal activities of which it becomes aware and responds to their requisitions, as the Law requires.

intellectualProperty.title: Intellectual property in the service
intellectualProperty.body: The name DIASPORA, its logo, its graphic identity, its interfaces and its software belong to the publisher or are used with the consent of their owners (see the Legal notice). These terms give you the right to use the service for your personal needs or those of your organisation; they transfer no right in these elements to you.

personalData.title: Personal data
personalData.body: The processing of your data is described in the Privacy page: data processed, purposes, recipients, retention periods, rights and how to exercise them. You export your data and request the erasure of your account from “My data”.

availability.title: Availability and development of the service
availability.body:
The publisher endeavours to keep the service accessible at all times, without guaranteeing it: maintenance, a breakdown or an incident at a provider may interrupt it. It may develop the service and open, change or close a space.

If the network were to stop, members would be warned in advance, in the network and by e-mail, and enabled to export their data.

liability.title: Liability

termination.title: Suspension and end of the account
termination.body:
You can at any time leave DIASPORA while keeping your ANTSIA account, or request the erasure of your whole account. Erasure begins 30 days after the request; until then, you can cancel it. After that period, it is final.

The publisher may suspend or close an account in the cases provided for by the Community rules, or when the account does not meet the conditions of access: a minor, a person who cannot enter the network, a second account, a false identity.

A suspended or excluded person keeps access to “My data”: they can read the decision there, appeal against it, export their data and request the erasure of their account.

changes.title: Changes to the terms
changes.body: Each version of these terms carries a number and a date, shown at the top of this page and in your settings. A significant change is announced in the network before it takes effect. Continuing to use the service after that date amounts to acceptance; if you refuse the new version, you can leave the network.

law.title: Applicable law and disputes
law.body:
These terms are subject to Gabonese law.

In the event of a dispute, write to the publisher first: it will reply to you and seek an amicable solution with you. You can also refer a complaint to the High Authority for Communication (Ordinance No. 0011/PR/2026, Article 38).

Failing agreement, the dispute falls within the jurisdiction of the courts of Libreville, subject to mandatory rules of jurisdiction. If you live in the European Union and act as a consumer, you keep the benefit of the mandatory provisions of the law of your country of residence and the possibility of bringing the matter before the courts of your domicile.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: For any question about these terms, write to {{publisherEmail}} or to {{publisherName}}, {{publisherAddress}}. The Contact page gives the other routes.

report.title: Reporting content
report.body:
Every post, comment, profile or page has a “Report…” action in its menu, like the other content on the network. Choose the reason: the moderation team examines the report, and the person reported does not know who reported them.

You follow your reports in “My reports”: acknowledgement of receipt, deadline where the law sets one, then decision. The Community rules give the time limits and the appeals.

emergency.title: In an emergency
emergency.body: A report does not alert the emergency services. If you or another person are in danger, call the emergency services of the country where you are: in the countries of the European Union, the emergency number 112.

messages.title: Writing to a member
messages.body: Contact between members goes through messaging, open between connections. No member’s e-mail address or telephone number is published, and the publisher passes none on.

data.title: Your data and your reports
data.body: Exporting your data, requesting the erasure of your account, following a moderation decision that concerns you, appealing against it or finding out the outcome of your reports: everything is done from “My data”, even without membership, after a departure or during a suspension.

publisher.title: Writing to the publisher

dataProtection.title: Personal data
dataProtection.body:
To exercise a right that “My data” does not cover (detailed access, rectification, restriction, objection) or to ask a question about the processing of your data, write to the publisher, by e-mail or by post, with the subject “Personal data — DIASPORA”.

Write from your account’s e-mail address: it is used to check that the request really comes from you. The reply is free of charge. It reaches you within one month of receipt of your request; this period may be extended by two months for a complex request, and you are then informed within the first month (Law No. 001/2011 as amended, Articles 93 and 95).

legalRequests.title: Authorities, right of reply and legal requests
legalRequests.body:
Judicial and administrative authorities send their notifications, requisitions and removal requests to the publisher, at its registered office or at {{publisherEmail}}. Exchanges are in French or English.

The right of reply of a person named in content is exercised at the same address, under the conditions set out in the Legal notice.

regulators.title: Supervisory authorities

consular.title: Consular procedures
consular.body: DIASPORA handles no consular procedure: passport, consular card, civil status, visa, legalisation. Contact the embassy or consulate of Gabon responsible for your place of residence. The publisher has no access to any consular file and cannot intervene in a procedure.
